# Gas Mining and Storage Gases are often consumed irreversibly. Whether they are lost to [textlink="space" link="Spacing"] or used in a burn chamber, the station must produce new gas to replace what was lost. The station must also store that gas safely and efficiently.
## Gas Miners Gas miners replenish the station's gas reserves. They are located in Atmospherics' gas storage chambers.
Gas miners constantly produce room-temperature gas and release it into the surrounding atmosphere. They require no power and never stop working until they reach their configured [bold]cutoff pressure[/bold].
More information about gas miners can be seen by examining them with [color=yellow][bold][keybind="ExamineEntity"][/bold][/color]. Try examining the gas miners shown above.
Gas miners have tiers: larger versions have a higher cutoff pressure than smaller ones.
If gas miners are ever unanchored from the station, they can be secured again with an ordinary wrench.
## Gas Storage Gas storage chambers hold gas produced by miners and supply it to other processes. They are located in Atmospherics.
[color=#999999][italic]Example of a small gas storage chamber[italic][/color]
Various atmospheric processes feed gases into storage chambers and draw them back out. For example: - Gas miners feed fresh gases into storage chambers whenever there is room. - The recycling network pumps recovered gases into storage chambers for reuse. - Systems such as the distronet and burn chamber draw gases from storage chambers.
Gas storage chambers are designed so that their contents can be measured with a [textlink="gas analyzer" link="AtmosTools"]. Because the output vent is a [textlink="passive vent" link="PassiveVent"], you can use a [textlink="gas analyzer" link="AtmosTools"] on the inlet of the [textlink="pump" link="Pumps"] that draws gas from the storage chamber to measure its contents.
